the earth, stained by the pollutions of ancient blood of beasts, sent up monthly griefs. Thus I emended the manuscript reading μηνεῖται ἄκη [it is angered, remedies]. He means beasts sent out each month for the purpose of avenging crimes. Other such monsters were believed to appear every year, like the sea-monster which destroyed both the people who encountered it and the crops that were produced, finally appeased when Hesione was thrown to it, as the scholia on Homer Il. 20, 145 and other writers cited by Heyne on Apollodorus vol. 2 p. 158 relate. The word ἄκη [remedies], which is in the manuscript, the copyist either introduced by chance or from the nearby words in v. 268 τούτων ἄκη τομαῖα καὶ λυτήρια | πράξας [having performed cutting and releasing remedies for these]. ἄχη [griefs] is used as in Ch. 585, where similarly about beasts it is said, πολλὰ μὲν γὰρ τρέφει δεινὰ δειμάτων ἄχη [for the earth nourishes many terrible griefs of fears].
